NO. 022 · Songbirds & City Birds / Cisticolidae · Cisticolas & Prinias

Zitting Cisticola

棕扇尾莺 · zōng shàn wěi yīng Cisticola juncidis
Resident Common 10–11 cm Protected (China) IUCN LC

Calls 'zit' with every bounce, like a wound-up toy

It has an unmistakable flight: bouncing through the air in steps, calling once per bounce, so the trajectory reads as a dotted line. Land, and it disappears into the grass for good.

Gallery

One scientific illustration for shape and colour blocks, two field photographs for how it looks in real light. Click any image to enlarge.

Identification

  • PlumageBrown above with heavy black streaking on the back; pale supercilium; underparts pale buff with a whiter throat.
  • TailShort and broad with clear white tips, fanned like a little fan — hence the name.
  • HeadCrown brown and finely streaked; bill short and thick, blunter than Plain Prinia's.
  • FlightThe display flight is a pronounced series of bounds, each rise accompanied by a call — the easiest way to confirm the species in the field.

Behaviour

Lives in tall grass, paddies and marsh edges, skulking low in the vegetation. In the breeding season the male sings on a bounding display flight to claim territory. Eats insects and grass seed. Present all year here, but sings hardest in spring and autumn.

Voice

A single 'zit' or 'zitting', short and nasal, given every second or two in flight with metronomic regularity — like a sewing machine, or something being wound up.

Where to find it in Zhuhai

  • Doumen grassy slopes
  • Jinwan rough grass
  • Hengqin wetland fringes
  • Qi'ao Island grassland
Field note
A small bird moving through the air in bounces, one call per bounce, can be identified on the spot — none of the other common warblers here fly like that.
